question.text: A Credit Risk Fund must invest a minimum of 65% of total assets in corporate debt instruments rated:

explanation.text: The Logic: Credit Risk Funds must invest a minimum of 65 percent of total assets in corporate debt instruments rated AA and below. By contrast, Corporate Bond Funds invest predominantly in instruments rated AA+ and above, making the two categories distinct on the rating axis. The Trap: The AA+ and above threshold belongs to Corporate Bond Funds. Credit Risk Funds deliberately take on lower-rated paper to earn higher yields. Note: Lower-rated debt is exposed to downgrade and spread risk, so the rating bucket is a defining feature of this category.
